title: Activepieces vs Dify: Features and Pricing (2026)
summary: Activepieces vs Dify address different needs: one automates work with governance, the other builds AI products. You'll know which fits your requirements.
body_markdown:
## Automation versus AI app building: the core job


Dify is the better fit for chatbots, RAG and LLM apps; Activepieces runs cross-app processes that include AI steps, across 746 integrations. The difference is where the work lives: inside a model-centred product, or across the systems a team already runs.


The diagram shows both shapes. On the left, a workflow step reaches into a CRM, email, a spreadsheet and chat, with an AI step as one node among them.


> The difference is where the work lives: inside a model-centred product, or across the systems a team already runs.


On the right, a single LLM app bundles a knowledge base, a model and a chat interface.


### Where Dify is the better choice


If the deliverable is the assistant itself, such as a support bot grounded in your documents, Dify's built for it. Retrieval, model selection and the chat front end sit in one place.


159,579 GitHub stars: that is where[Gitstarclub](https://gitstarclub.com/langgenius/dify) 's[Github-Ranking-AI](https://github.com/yuxiaopeng/Github-Ranking-AI/blob/main/Top100/RAG.md) list puts Dify. It puts Flowise, another LLM app builder, at 55,537.


That means Dify has the Has more examples, answered issues and third-party guides than the other two here.


### Where Activepieces is the better choice


**25,286 stars** is what Activepieces has on the same list, and its MIT-licensed core carries 746 integrations, **roughly 60% of them community-contributed** , meaning most of the integration library is built by developers outside the core team.


That's a smaller community, and it shouldn't be read as a weaker tool for this job.


When the task is "a form arrives, the CRM updates, a model drafts a reply, the team gets a chat message," the product's the process, not a chat window.


A process like that grows agents, integrations, shared team data, an AI chat and approvals, and Activepieces keeps all of it in one product, so access, history and releases are handled in one place: custom RBAC, SSO, SCIM, audit logs, event streaming, environments and git sync, on cloud or self-hosted.


MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run it in production. Assemble that span from point tools and you have six vendors, six bills and six separate places to look when a run breaks.


### Using both together


The two aren't mutually exclusive. A team can build a knowledge-base assistant in Dify and call it from a workflow as one step.


The workflow handles triggers, routing and writes to other apps, while Dify handles the retrieval and answer. The cost is two systems to monitor and two sets of credentials, so it pays off only when both jobs actually exist.
